newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rises to 9.0 pct in tight market.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rises to 9.0 pct in tight market.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to as high as 9.0 percent on Tuesday as local banks continued to cover their short positions, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 8.0 and 8.5 percent on Monday.
Dealers said the market remained tight due to a mismatch of funds, held mostly by foreign banks.
"The market is still tight as money is not spread among market players. The foreign banks are long while local banks are short," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said banks also kept funds for payment for a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue on Wednesday.
Bank Negara earlier announced that it accepted bids at an average yield of 6.427 percent, against 6.955 percent at the auction of 30-day bills amounting to 500 million ringgit on May 20.
Earlier, one- and two-week money were at 8.0/8.50 percent against 7.70/80 on Monday.
The one-month rate was at 8.0/8.20 percent from 7.60/90 while three-month money was at 8.0/8.10 percent against 7.50/80.
Dealers said they expected rates to stay firm through the week.
One dealer said it was possible that the rates were kept high by Bank Negara as a move to fend off a fresh speculative attack on the ringgit.
"The nine percent offered (for the overnight) today may have been taken by Bank Negara," he said.
No confirmation was available as the central bank does not comment on its money market operations.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange extended losses on further liquidation following the firmness in the cash market, futures dealers said.
At 0830 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down eight points to 92.34, or an implied yield of 7.66 percent.
September contract fell four to 92.51, or 7.49 percent.
